segments.method: sum of the City-published adjacent segments

notes: The City map marks all three as designated public river access points and says Lions Park is the end of navigable river segments.
The City map marks Among the Waters as walk-in access only.
A 2024 New Mexico fish-tissue study provides in-river sample coordinates for Westland Park and Lions Park; these were selected as initial on-water markers and require endpoint snapping review.

westlandPark.source: 2024 fish-tissue study; San Juan River sampling reach

kirtlandLionsPark.source: 2024 fish-tissue study; San Juan River sampling reach

gauge.siteName: San Juan River at Farmington, NM

scoring.disclaimer: Flow values are score preferences from a community guide, not safe-to-run limits. The City asks river users to check current flows, hazards and weather.

safety: Farmington signage requires Coast Guard-approved PFDs, asks users to check flows, hazards and weather, and says difficulty changes with water level.
Farmington designates public access points only, asks users to stay in their watercraft and on the water, and lists park/access hours.
Route notes cover low or changing water, unknown features, weather, heat, cold-water shock, private banks and limited exits.

camping.notes: These are day-float options. No authorized on-route campsite is confirmed; no camping at access points or private banks is implied.

notes: Among-Waters to Westland and Westland to Lions are the two adjacent City-published legs.
Among-Waters to Lions is their longer combined option and shares river miles with the Westland-to-Lions shorter launch alternative.
Among-Waters to Lions starts at the existing Vereda-to-Among route's takeout and is an adjacent, non-overlapping downstream continuation.

gallery.notes: Visually reviewed same-river view near Navajo Dam, roughly 40 river miles upstream. Captions state that it is corridor context, not an endpoint or current-condition photo.

requiredChecks: audit endpoint snaps for all three routes
